def: A quantity of storage in an NVM subsystem, formatted and addressed independently and identified by an NSID; each namespace uses one I/O command set (NVM, ZNS, KV, SLM or Computational Programs).
32-bit identifier of a namespace within one NVM subsystem, carried in Command Dword 1 of every SQE. 0h means no namespace; FFFFFFFFh is the broadcast value; it is not globally unique.

Value that names a namespace's I/O command set: 00h NVM, 01h Key Value, 02h Zoned Namespace, 03h Subsystem Local Memory, 04h Computational Programs (as encoded in libnvme; confirm in the Base specification).
Allowing a namespace's size (NSZE) to exceed the capacity actually reserved for it (NCAP), so that writes to never-written blocks can fail when the pool is exhausted. Reported by NSFEAT bit 0.
A descriptor in Identify Namespace giving metadata size (MS), block size as a power of two (LBADS) and relative performance (RP); FLBAS selects which descriptor a namespace uses.
Admin command (opcode 0Dh) that creates (SEL 0h) or deletes (SEL 1h) namespaces; a successful create returns the new NSID in completion Dword 0.
Admin command (opcode 15h) that attaches (SEL 0h) or detaches (SEL 1h) a namespace to or from the controllers named in a Controller List; only attached namespaces are active on a controller.

128-bit globally unique namespace identifier reported in Identify Namespace and the Namespace Identification Descriptor list; hosts use it to recognise the same namespace through different controllers.
64-bit globally unique namespace identifier based on an IEEE company identifier, reported in Identify Namespace and the descriptor list.
128-bit UUID for a namespace, reported only through the Namespace Identification Descriptor list (descriptor type 3h).
Per-controller reporting of path state (Optimized, Non-Optimized, Inaccessible, Persistent Loss, Change) for groups of namespaces, used by multipath hosts; reported in the ANA log page.
A collection of NVM media whose wear is managed and reported together (Endurance Group Information log); contains one or more NVM Sets.
A performance-isolated subset of an endurance group's media; the basis of Predictable Latency Mode. Each namespace belongs to one NVM Set when sets are supported.
A namespace using the Zoned Namespace Command Set (CSI 02h), whose LBAs are divided into zones that must be written sequentially and reset as a whole.
A fixed-size range of LBAs in a zoned namespace with its own write pointer, capacity and state (Empty, Implicitly/Explicitly Opened, Closed, Full, Read Only, Offline).
The next LBA that may be written in a zone; writes must start exactly there, and it advances by the blocks written. Not valid in Full, Read Only or Offline zones.
Number of writable logical blocks in a zone, reported per zone; may be smaller than the zone size and may shrink over the device's life.
ZNS I/O command (opcode 7Dh) that writes data at a zone's current write pointer and returns the LBA of the first written block in completion Dwords 0-1, allowing many writes to one zone in flight.
Maximum data size of a Zone Append, reported in the ZNS Identify Controller structure as a power of two in units of the minimum memory page size; 0 means MDTS applies.
ZNS Identify Namespace field: the maximum number of zones that may be implicitly or explicitly opened at once (0's based; all ones means no limit).
ZNS Identify Namespace field: the maximum number of zones that may be opened or closed (partially written) at once (0's based; all ones means no limit).
A namespace using the Key Value Command Set (CSI 01h) that stores variable-size values under short byte-string keys with Store, Retrieve, Delete, Exist and List commands.
KV Store option: store only if the key already exists (update-only); otherwise the command fails with KV Key Does Not Exist.
KV Store option: store only if the key does not exist (create-only); otherwise the command fails with Key Exists.

Running computation inside or next to a storage device so data is processed where it lives and only results cross the host interface; in NVMe, the Computational Programs and Subsystem Local Memory command sets.
A namespace using the Computational Programs Command Set; it holds programs at program indexes and is the target of Execute Program.
Code executed by a compute engine in an NVMe subsystem; either device-defined (preloaded) or downloaded with Load Program and enabled with Program Activation Management.
A namespace using the Subsystem Local Memory Command Set: byte-addressable memory inside the NVM subsystem used, for example, as working memory for computational programs.
A set of ranges (memory namespace, offset, length) created with Memory Range Set Management; an Execute Program names one and the program may access only those ranges.
NVMe command set (CSI 03h) that exposes byte-addressable memory in the NVM subsystem as memory namespaces, with commands to read, write and copy data into and out of it.
